## 1601 N Milwaukee Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN 14313320180000 | West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2 (Community Shopping District)**, per the City's official GIS parcel records. The district was set by ordinance #17230, dated May 4, 2011; the map record was last updated December 15, 2021. No recent rezoning has occurred.

**Verify:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) or the Cook County parcel lookup using PIN 14313320180000.

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail + Apartments Above — Allowed?

**Yes, permitted by right.** [1] describes B3 as accommodating "a very broad range of retail and service uses." [2] (the use table) confirms dwelling units above the ground floor are a **permitted (P)** use in B3 districts. Ground-floor residential is more restricted — dwelling units *below* the second floor require review — but commercial/retail on the ground floor with residential above is the paradigmatic B3 use.

**Verify:** [2] (§ 17-3-0200, use table row 3–4); [1] (§ 17-3-0104).

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures come from the zoning table for B3-2 (§ [1]):

| Standard | Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | **2.2** |
| **Max height** | **45–50 ft** (varies by lot frontage & ground-floor commercial) |
| **Min lot area per dwelling unit** | **1,000 sq ft** |
| **Lot coverage** | Not specified in retrieved standards |
| **Setbacks** | Not specified in retrieved standards |

**Unit yield:** With 11,951 sq ft of lot area, lot-area-per-unit math yields a maximum of **11 dwelling units** (11,951 ÷ 1,000 = 11 units). *Important caveat: this is a lot-area ceiling only — FAR, height, and parking may constrain the actual buildable count further. Efficiency and SRO units count at smaller per-unit areas and could allow more units* (see the density table).

**Verify:** §17-3-0104 and the bulk table at §17-3-0401 in the Municipal Code (current through Council Journal of March 18, 2026 — a later amendment may not be reflected).

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

This parcel carries **multiple significant overlays**:

- **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — City-designated historic district. Exterior alterations will require review by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
- **Individual Landmark Building** — This specific building (historically recorded as "Noel State Bank," CHRS rating: orange) is flagged as an individual landmark. This is the most restrictive overlay: demolition and exterior changes face heightened scrutiny from the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
- **Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — Listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Federal designation does not restrict private development directly, but it unlocks **Historic Tax Credits** for qualifying rehabilitation projects and signals heightened local sensitivity.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — Within a CTA TOD overlay (see §5 below).
- **ADU Eligible Area** — Accessory Dwelling Units may be established on this parcel per the City's ADU pilot program.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any qualifying residential project triggers ARO affordability obligations. West Town community area has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 units in this zone.
- **Wicker Park Special Service Area (SSA)** — The parcel sits within the Wicker Park SSA, which levies a supplemental property tax for neighborhood services (currently costing this parcel ~$2,363/year in SSA 33 levy).
- **No Planned Development** overlay applies; the parcel is not in a PMD, lakefront protection zone, or special manufacturing district.
- **FEMA Flood Zone X** — Area of minimal flood hazard; flood insurance is not required.
- **Nearby brownfield:** PARK 512 AVENUE PARK (EPA ID 110005863100, ~0.2 mi). Environmental due diligence may be advisable.

**Verify:** Commission on Chicago Landmarks (312-744-3200); City GIS overlays; National Register via Illinois SHPO.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Relief

B3 districts are generally destination-oriented with higher parking expectations [1]. However, this parcel is **transit-served** — it sits within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station (Damen Blue Line, just 0.07 miles away). Under §17-10-0102-B, **the minimum parking requirement can be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning no off-street parking is required for this location [4]. This is a significant by-right benefit requiring no special entitlement.

**Note:** No density, FAR, or height bonus applies at B3-2; those transit bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (B1-3, B2-3, etc.) under §17-3-0402-B and related sections.

**Verify:** §17-10-0102-B; [4] (§17-3-0308, transit-served criteria).

---

### 6. Demolition & New Mixed-Use Construction — What's Required?

This is the most complex question given the overlays. Here is the sequence of approvals:

**a) Landmark review (critical barrier):** The building is flagged as an **Individual Landmark Building** and sits within the Milwaukee Avenue Historic District. Demolition of a Chicago landmark requires approval from the **Commission on Chicago Landmarks** and ultimately City Council. This is a high bar — outright demolition of a designated landmark is rarely approved. You must determine whether the landmark designation is fully enacted (the ordinance number was not in the retrieved data — confirm with the Commission).

**b) National Register (federal):** Does not legally block demolition for private projects, but triggers Section 106 review if any federal permits, licenses, or funding are involved.

**c) Zoning compliance:** A new mixed-use building (retail ground floor + residential above) is permitted by right under B3-2 [1][2]. New construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station must comply with transit-served location criteria [4] (§17-3-0308), including pedestrian-street standards at §17-3-0504 even if not on a designated pedestrian street.

**d) ARO obligation:** A new residential project in this ARO zone will trigger affordability requirements. Consult DHED for the applicable set-aside percentage.

**e) Planned Development threshold:** Check whether the project's size (FAR, height, or units) triggers mandatory PD review under §17-8-0500. At 2.2 FAR on ~11,951 sq ft, the maximum buildable floor area is ~26,292 sq ft — verify whether this crosses PD thresholds.

**f) Wrecking permit:** A demolition permit from the Department of Buildings is required regardless.

**Verify:** Commission on Chicago Landmarks (312-744-3200) for landmark status; §17-8-0500 for PD thresholds; §17-3-0308 for transit-served criteria; DHED for ARO.

---

### Confidence & Limitations

**High confidence:** Zoning district, FAR, height, lot-area-per-unit, use permissions, parking reduction, TOD/ADU/ARO/SSA overlays, and flood zone — all from authoritative city GIS and the Municipal Code (current through March 18, 2026).

**Moderate confidence:** Landmark status — the data flags this as an individual landmark building, but the specific designating ordinance and effective date were not in the retrieved data. This must be confirmed directly with the Commission on Chicago Landmarks before any demolition or exterior alteration planning.

**Could not determine:** Setbacks, lot coverage maximums, and whether the project crosses mandatory PD thresholds — these require the full bulk table at §17-3-0401 and §17-8-0500, which were not in the retrieved code text.
